haiku-low.q1: A pull request builds the image without pushing and runs unit tests only; it never deploys. A merge to main starts deploying runs.
haiku-low.q2: Staging and production deploy shop-api:<commit SHA>, the image built once per run. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
haiku-low.q3: An integration test failure gets one automatic retry, then ends the run if it fails again. A unit test failure ends the run immediately, with no retry. Nothing reaches staging.
haiku-low.q4: Staging runs the image it ran before this run, restored by deploy.sh rollback staging. It is found via SSM /deploy/staging/previous_tag.
haiku-low.q5: Only release-approvers members who are not the commit author may approve. With no approval in 72 hours, the run expires, nothing reaches production, and staging keeps its image.
haiku-low.q6: In SSM Parameter Store, under /deploy/<env>/current_tag and previous_tag. Only deploy.sh writes them, after a successful stable rollout or a rollback. Canary is never recorded.
haiku-low.q7: Stable is untouched, SSM is unchanged, and the schema stays migrated, since migrations are forward-only and not reverted. Canary-off runs and the lock is released.
haiku-low.q8: The older run is cancelled as superseded, and it posts a notice to #deploys. This includes runs waiting for approval, the window or the lock.
haiku-low.q9: It waits, re-checking every 5 minutes until it is inside Mon-Thu 09:00-15:00 UTC and the production lock is free. Approvals do not expire.
haiku-low.q10: The canary's 5xx ratio is measured from Prometheus every 60 seconds for 15 minutes. One reading above 1%, or no data, fails it immediately.
haiku-low.q11: The run posts a waiting-for-approval notice to #deploys. It includes IMAGE_TAG, a link to smoke results, and commits between production current_tag and IMAGE_TAG.
haiku-low.q12: Staging and production use kubectl rollout undo, which returns pods to the previous running image; SSM is unchanged on failure. For staging, rollback is avoided because previous_tag would go one version too far back. Production's reason is NOT STATED.

sonnet.q1: A pull request runs build (image not pushed) and unit tests only, posting status on the PR; it never deploys. A merge to main starts the full pipeline.
sonnet.q2: Both deploy the single image registry.internal/shop-api:<commit SHA> (IMAGE_TAG), built once per run. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
sonnet.q3: Integration test failure gets one automatic retry; if the retry fails, the run fails. Unit test failure gets no retry and fails the run immediately. Any final failure ends the run, posts the failing step to the deploys channel, and nothing reaches staging.
sonnet.q4: Staging runs the image it ran before this run. deploy.sh rollback staging sets current_tag back to previous_tag, read from SSM Parameter Store (/deploy/staging/previous_tag). The failure is then posted to the deploys channel.
sonnet.q5: A member of release-approvers who is not the commit author, approving in the CI UI. If no approval within 72 hours of reaching the gate, the run expires: it posts to the deploys channel, nothing goes to production, and staging keeps the image.
sonnet.q6: In SSM Parameter Store, outside the pipeline, at /deploy/<env>/current_tag and /deploy/<env>/previous_tag. Only deploy.sh writes them: after a successful stable rollout (deploy.sh <env> <tag>), and on rollback (current_tag set back to previous_tag). The canary is never recorded.
sonnet.q7: Stable deployment untouched, SSM tags unchanged, and the schema stays migrated (migrations are not reverted). deploy.sh canary-off removes the canary, then the lock is released and the failure is posted.
sonnet.q8: The older run is cancelled as superseded and posts a notice, whether it was waiting for approval, the window, or the lock, as long as it had not started its production deploy.
sonnet.q9: It waits and re-checks every 5 minutes until it is inside the start window (Mon-Thu 09:00-15:00 UTC) and the production lock is free. The approval does not expire (e.g. Thursday evening approval starts Monday 09:00). Once started, the deploy may run past 15:00.
sonnet.q10: The canary's 5xx ratio is measured. The canary-watch step queries Prometheus every 60 seconds for 15 minutes. Failure is any single reading above 1% or a query returning no data, which fails it at once and triggers canary-off.
sonnet.q11: The run posts to the #deploys channel (waiting for approval notice) with IMAGE_TAG, a link to the smoke results, and the commits between production current_tag and IMAGE_TAG.
sonnet.q12: Both use kubectl rollout undo (in production, followed by canary-off), which returns to the pods that were running. rollback is not used because SSM was not written, so previous_tag would go one version too far back; SSM still names the old image. Migrations are not reverted, so rollback swaps the image only.
